interface.name: weston_pinned_windows_v1

description.summary: runtime control of desktop-shell pinned-window rules

interface.description:
Mutates the desktop-shell pinned-window rule table at runtime. Clients stage rules with add_rule and clear, then atomically swap the staged set into the live table with commit.
WARNING: any connected client may bind this interface and remap arbitrary windows. It is the moral equivalent of weston_debug_v1 and MUST NOT be exposed in untrusted environments.
Rule semantics mirror the [pinned-window] sections of weston.ini: first-match-wins, NULL or empty app_id / title fields are wildcards, width or height of 0 means "leave the surface's intrinsic size". The x, y, width, height values are in global compositor coordinates (the same coordinate space used by weston_view_set_position). On commit the staged set fully replaces any prior rules (including any loaded from weston.ini at startup); merging is not supported.
Pinned surfaces are also sent the xdg-shell maximized state and all four tiled_* edge states in their configure so cooperating clients (GTK, Qt, libdecor, SDL) suppress client-side decorations. Clients that ignore these signals may still draw their own decorations. When a commit removes a previously-pinned surface from the rule table, these signals are cleared on the next configure so the client may restore its decorations.

entry.name: invalid_match
entry.summary: all four matcher fields were null or empty

request.name: destroy
request.description: Discards any rules staged on this resource. The live table is left untouched.

request.name: add_rule

description.summary: append a rule to the staged set

request.description:
Appends one rule. Each of the four matcher fields (app_id, title, x11_wm_class, x11_wm_name) is independent: a null or empty field is a wildcard, a non-empty field must equal the corresponding surface attribute. app_id / title come from xdg-shell; x11_wm_class / x11_wm_name come from the X11 WM_CLASS / WM_NAME properties and let rules target Xwayland clients (whose xdg app_id is typically empty in Weston).
All four matcher fields null/empty is a protocol error (invalid_match). Negative width or height is invalid_size. Width or height of 0 keeps the surface's intrinsic size.

description.summary: drop all rules staged on this resource

request.name: commit

description.summary: atomically replace the live rule table

request.description: Swaps the staged set into the shell's live rule table, re-evaluates every mapped surface in a single pass, and re-initialises the staged set so the same resource can build the next batch. Servers respond with one applied event.

event.name: applied

description.summary: server swapped in a new rule table

event.description: Fired once per successful commit. count is the number of rules now live.
